_about: Placement evidence rules derived from the consolidated literature review (8 Nov 2026). Coordinates for size M: z = height above hem (mm), BNP at z = 700; dcb = surface distance from centre back; dcf = surface distance from centre front; 'side' = which half of the torso (back if dcb < C/4). Regions are tested in order; first match wins. Scores 0-1 are the team's reading of the evidence, not published values.

c7t2: Insulated skin temperature at C7-T2 was the single strongest predictor of rectal temperature (SEE 0.27 °C).
interscap: Insulated scapula skin temperature + heart rate estimated core with SEE 0.29 °C; scapula skin temperature + HR Kalman filter RMSE 0.25 °C.
Eggenberger et al., 2018; Welles et al., 2018
scapula: Scapula site: SEE 0.29 °C with HR (insulated); RMSE 0.25 °C in a Kalman filter.
Eggenberger et al., 2018; Welles et al., 2018
pectoral: Pectoralis gave the lowest Kalman-filter error (RMSE 0.18 °C with skin temp, heat flux and HR). Watch for vest coverage.
sternum: Sternum RMSE 0.20 °C with skin temp, heat flux and HR; chest skin + HR classified PSI >= 7.5 with 10% error.
Welles et al., 2018; Buller et al., 2008
xiphoid: Rib-cage site RMSE 0.18 °C with skin temp, heat flux and HR.
midback: Trunk site between validated upper-back and lower sites, but not tested directly in the reviewed studies.
lowback: Not tested in the reviewed core-estimation studies; under the pack back panel.
shoulder_top: Close to C7 but under shoulder straps; not a tested site.
abdomen: Not a tested site; skin flaps and belt movement.
side: Not a tested site; arm movement and airflow disturb skin temperature.
hem: Not a tested site; hip-belt band.

lowback: Reference site for trunk gait algorithms; valid and reliable for stride variables; regularity ICC 0.69-0.83.
Moe-Nilssen & Helbostad, 2004; Del Din et al., 2016; Horsley et al., 2021; Kobayashi et al., 2014
sternum: The only heat-stroke prediction studies used a chest sensor; chest agrees with lumbar on mean gait values but not on variability or asymmetry.
Buller et al., 2022; Yaldiz et al., 2023; Camerlingo et al., 2024; Del Din et al., 2016
xiphoid: Chest site as used by Buller et al. (2022); mean gait values agree with lumbar.
Buller et al., 2022; Camerlingo et al., 2024
pectoral: Chest, but off-midline: more arm and breathing motion.
Del Din et al., 2016; team assessment
midback: Trunk site between validated thoracic and lumbar sites; not directly validated.
interscap: Upper-trunk harmonic ratio predicted falls (AUC 0.81); thoracic stride-event evidence unclear; anteroposterior harmonic ratio damped from pelvis to shoulder (8.85 to 5.48).
Doi et al., 2013; Horsley et al., 2021; Mazzà et al., 2008
c7t2: C7 is the upper-trunk site of Doi et al. (AUC 0.81), but damping is largest near the shoulders.
Doi et al., 2013; Mazzà et al., 2008
scapula: Scapula moves with the arm and shoulder girdle; not validated for gait.
shoulder_top: No gait validation found for a shoulder-top sensor; shoulder-girdle and weapon-handling motion add non-gait acceleration.
abdomen: Near the pelvis but on soft tissue; not validated.
side: Arm swing contaminates the signal; not validated.
hem: Near the pelvis but loose hem and hip belt; not validated.
sleeve: Wrist-hip stride variability agreement only rho 0.36-0.52; wrist detects walking less well than the lower back.
Urbanek et al., 2018; Kluge et al., 2024

c7t2: Highest regional sweat rate was on the upper back.
interscap: Highest regional sweat rate was on the upper back.
scapula: Upper back: highest regional sweat rates.
lowback: Back sweats more than limbs; below the upper-back maximum.
sternum: Torso front sweats heavily but less than the upper back.
pectoral: Torso front; lower than upper back.
xiphoid: Torso front; lower than upper back.
abdomen: Torso front; lower than upper back.
shoulder_top: Not a mapped maximum; strap rubbing.
side: Lateral torso sweats less than the central back.
sleeve: Limbs sweat less than the torso.

xiphoid: Lower-chest band position used by ECG shirts; textile ECG is limited mainly by motion artefact.
pectoral: Across the heart, but more arm and pectoral muscle noise.
Pedrini Schuch et al., 2026; team assessment
sternum: Too close to the other electrode for a strong lead signal.
side: Lateral chest still spans the heart; more arm motion.
abdomen: Further from the heart: lower amplitude.
midback: Back placement gives lower ECG amplitude; not in the reviewed studies.
interscap: Back placement gives lower ECG amplitude.
scapula: Back placement gives lower ECG amplitude.
shoulder_top: Far from the heart; strap rubbing.

c7t2: No physiological constraint. Short traces to an upper-back patch; reachable by the section commander.
interscap: Short traces, but a 13 mm pod sits under the pack back panel.
scapula: Under straps or pack panel; shoulder-blade motion.
pectoral: Soldier can feel and see it; covered by a vest.
sternum: Visible and accessible; covered by a vest.
xiphoid: Accessible; long traces to back sensors.
lowback: Under the pack and near the hip belt.
side: Clear of pack and vest, but arm swing knocks it.

upper_arm_outer: Upper-arm optical HR: bias -0.05 bpm, MAPE 1.35% vs chest-strap ECG.
upper_arm_inner: Upper arm, but sleeve rubbing near the axilla.
torso: Optical HR pod is designed for the upper arm (wrist MAPE 6.82% was much worse).
